From: Office of the Chief Financial Officer. Date: March 12, 2025. Subject: proposed operating budget for fiscal year 2025, for approval at the March 20 Board meeting.

1. Summary

The proposed operating expense budget for FY2025 is $268 million, an increase of 12% over FY2024 actual operating expenses of $239 million. Capital expenditure is budgeted at $34 million, mainly for data-center capacity in Frankfurt and Virginia.

2. Operating Expenses by Function

Research and development: $112 million.

Sales and marketing: $98 million.

General and administrative: $58 million.

3. Headcount

The plan adds 220 net new employees over the year, 60% of them in research and development. Most hires are planned for the second half of the year.

4. Cost Measures

The company-wide travel budget is reduced by 10% compared to FY2024. External consulting spend is capped at $9 million. Any new spend above the approved budget for a function requires approval from the Chief Financial Officer.

5. Risks

The budget assumes revenue growth at the midpoint of guidance, about 15.5%. If growth falls below 14%, the hiring plan for the second half will be reduced by up to half.

[4] ## Revenue

Total revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $482.0 million, an increase of 18.4% compared to $407.1 million in fiscal year 2023. The year-over-year growth was propelled by:

- Enterprise Cloud subscription revenue of $312.7 million (up 24.1% YoY).
- Managed Services revenue of $128.6 million (up 11.2% YoY).
- Other revenue of $40.7 million, roughly flat versus the prior year.

The revenue mix continues to shift toward recurring subscription revenue, which represented 84.6% of total revenue in FY2024, compared to 79.3% in FY2023.

[9] # Employee Handbook

This handbook summarizes the principal policies for employees of Acme Corporation. It is an internal document and does not form part of any customer agreement.

## Paid Time Off
Employees are entitled to twenty-five (25) days of paid time off per calendar year, accruing monthly. Up to five (5) unused days may be carried over into the following year.

## Working Model
Acme operates a hybrid working model. Employees must work from the office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with core collaboration hours between 10:00 and 16:00 local time.

## Probation
New employees serve a probationary period of three (3) months, during which either party may end the employment with one (1) week's notice.

## Notice of Resignation
After probation, employees are asked to give at least one (1) month's written notice of resignation.

## Business Expenses
Pre-approved business expenses are reimbursed within thirty (30) days of a complete expense claim.

[10] ### 1.3 Termination for Cause

Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within fifteen (15) days after receiving written notice of the breach.

[11] ## 3. Support Response Times
Provider responds to support requests according to severity:

- Priority 1 (critical, service unavailable): within one (1) hour.
- Priority 2 (high, major feature impaired): within four (4) business hours.
- Priority 3 (normal): within one (1) business day.

## 4. Scheduled Maintenance
Routine maintenance is performed on Sundays between 02:00 and 06:00 UTC. Provider gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' advance notice of any scheduled maintenance, which does not count against the uptime commitment.

[1] ## 1. Gifts and Hospitality

Employees may accept gifts or hospitality from business partners only when the value does not exceed US$100 per person per year and the gift is not cash or a cash equivalent. Any gift above that value must be declined or reported to the Compliance team. Gifts may never be offered to government officials without prior approval from Legal.

[2] ## 1. Approval Thresholds

Every purchase requires a purchase order approved according to its total contract value:

- below US$10,000: the requester's manager;
- from US$10,000 to US$100,000: a Director and the Finance business partner;
- above US$100,000 and up to US$500,000: the Chief Financial Officer;
- above US$500,000: the Chief Executive Officer, after review by the Chief Financial Officer.

## 2. Competitive Quotes

Purchases above US$50,000 require at least three (3) written quotes, unless the supplier is the only one able to provide the goods or services. A sole-source justification must then be attached to the purchase order.

## 3. Vendor Onboarding

New suppliers are onboarded by the Procurement team. A supplier that will access company or customer data must also pass the security review described in the Information Security Policy before the contract is signed.

## 4. Payment Terms

Acme's standard payment term for suppliers is forty-five (45) days from the invoice date. Shorter terms require approval from the Finance business partner.

## 5. Splitting Purchases

Splitting a purchase into smaller orders to avoid an approval threshold is prohibited.

[3] ## 2. Home Office Support

Each employee receives a one-time home office stipend of US$500 and a monthly internet allowance of US$50. Company equipment, including the laptop and one external monitor, remains company property and must be returned at the end of employment.

The aggregate liability of Provider arising out of or related to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, shall not exceed one million United States dollars ($1,000,000) or the total fees paid by Customer to Provider under the applicable Order Form during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim, whichever is greater.

3. Hotels

The nightly hotel rate, excluding taxes, may not exceed US$250. In New York, London and San Francisco the limit is US$325 per night. Employees must use the preferred hotels listed in the booking tool when one is available.

4. Meals

5. Ground Transportation

Employees should use public transport or taxis. Rental cars are allowed when cheaper than the alternatives or when traveling with colleagues. Use of a personal car is reimbursed at US$0.67 per mile.

6. Receipts and Submission

An itemized receipt is required for every expense of US$25 or more. Expense claims must be submitted within thirty (30) days after the trip ends. Claims submitted more than ninety (90) days after the trip are not reimbursed.

7. Non-reimbursable Expenses

The following are not reimbursed: upgrades paid for personally, airline lounge memberships, traffic and parking fines, personal entertainment, and expenses for a spouse or family member.

Employees who travel more than four (4) times per year are issued a corporate card. Personal expenses must never be charged to it.
